summary: Three messages all week, none of them from her. Hailey has not typed a word since 'Just sent it over' at 14:57 on 8/20 - 7 days 18 hours of silence at week close - and ALTR produced exactly three messages in seven days: Michelle's automated leak-removal recap on 8/25, a two-word 'Thank you!' from Stephski on 8/26, and one question from Mayson at 22:06 on 8/27. That is the entire account this week. The 'Thank you!' is the closest thing she has been given to confirmation that her 8/20 wire landed, six days after she sent it, and it does not say the money arrived or which account it arrived in - compare 5/20, when Stephski wrote 'Hi Haleigh we recieved your wire' in plain words. Stephski still has never answered the question Hailey asked on 8/18 about which account to use; it is now 10 days unanswered by the person who sent the invoice, and she only got an answer at all because Derrek stepped in and told her to ignore the invoice. Mayson's message is the week's real finding. He asked 'Hey Haleigh how come you're not using the domain on instagram?' - 75 days after she told him the answer. On 6/11 he sold her the .vip domain as protection 'from shadow bans or account restrictions related to your link' and assured her 'Yes It's safe to put it in bio'. On 6/13 she came back with 'One of my accounts already hit a restriction with it' and 'And my other one did too'. On 6/14 he wrote 'Working on it' and has said nothing about it since. Asking her why she is not using a product that restricted two of her accounts, without ever closing the loop, is the single clearest example on this account of ALTR not reading its own chat. Everything else simply aged: the 7/29 shadowban ask is 30 days old with Vivek still on 1 message in 754, Derrek's 'plenty of updates starting next week' phone-farm promise is 27 days old, the named-account-manager ask is 128 days old, the emoticon ban is 155 days old, and Ronnie's 8/18 fan resolution still has no closing confirmation. Nobody chased anything. Nobody proactively told her anything. Zero client messages is not a crisis for her - she has gone 12, 14 and 16 days quiet before - but it is the second zero-client week in three, and this time there was no invoice to hide behind.

health.rationale: Down 7 from 65 (and 68, 80 before that) - a fourth consecutive decline, and the first one caused by nothing happening rather than something going wrong. Last week's 3-point slip was punishment for a live failure on a money question. This week there was no failure because there was no work: 3 messages, 0 from her, and only one of ALTR's three was written by a human thinking about her account. Every open item aged by exactly seven days and not one was touched - shadowban 23 to 30 days, phone-farm update 20 to 27, account manager 121 to 128, emoticons 148 to 155, and the .vip domain breakage Mayson said he was 'Working on it' on 6/14 hit 75 days. Two items got actively worse: Stephski's 'Thank you!' on 8/26 is the only acknowledgement of a wire sent six days earlier and still does not confirm which account received it, and Mayson's 8/27 question puts the burden of the failed .vip rollout back on the client. Held above the mid-50s only because she raised no new complaint, she is not showing exit signals (this silence length is normal for her), the payment appears to have landed, and Michelle's leak-removal recap shipped on time for the umpteenth week. If the 9/1 invoice cycle repeats the account-number ambiguity, or if she comes back and finds the shadowban still untouched at 35+ days, this drops into the 40s.
